review_notes:
I read the whole file. I grepped Mathlib for other definitions of the `RestrictScalars` type alias and for uses of `RestrictScalars.addEquiv`, `RestrictScalars.ringEquiv` and `RestrictScalars.lsmul`. The only definition site is this file, and the other uses are in Representation theory, Normed module and Lie base change files. I found no independent competing type synonym or structure for the same concept.

`RestrictScalars` is the Mathlib type synonym for restricting scalars. `Module.restrictScalars` and `Algebra.restrictScalars` are thin named wrappers over `Module.compHom` and `Algebra.compHom`, and the file documents why. The rubric says named specialisations are not defects. `addEquiv` and `ringEquiv` are deliberate wrappers over `AddEquiv.refl` and `RingEquiv.refl`, whose purpose is to stop instances leaking. `RestrictScalars.lsmul` is a named specialisation of `Algebra.lsmul`. I did not look further into the sibling `restrictScalars` APIs for bundled maps (`LinearMap.restrictScalars` and so on). They are listed in the docstring as different concepts. The practical case for consolidation is unclear, so I abstain.
